identity.real_world_identity_notes: British mid-engined sports prototype built by MCR Race Cars to Sports 2000 specification, running a two-litre Ford Duratec of about 200 bhp.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and no automatic blip on downshifts. The downshift was accepted with no pedal input, so no blip is needed to engage the gear.
The clutch is needed to pull away.

The source offers two gearbox makes for the car and does not say which this specification carries. Both are five-speed sequentials, which is what the drive found, so the gear count and construction stand while the make is not claimed.
The only five-speed car in this batch; its classmates all selected six.
The car does not blip its own downshifts. An earlier drive recorded that it did, from a measurement that could read the driver's throttle as the car's blip.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mcr-s2000.20260817t044512882z-83f67c74 by Jason Kinslow.

The automatic blip was re-measured on 2026-08-18 in AMS2 1.6.9.91, observation ams2.mcr-s2000.20260818t042136047z-843e9442. The car does not blip: the first reading was the old measurement seeing throttle carried in before the lift. The downshift was still accepted with no pedal input, so no blip is needed to engage the gear.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the MCR S2 and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The source gives a Sadev or Hewland five-speed sequential gearbox, and the live drive selected five sequential gears with an automatic cut and no automatic blip.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

deviations.basis: Five forward gears against the archetype's six. The source offers two gearbox makes for the car and does not say which this specification carries, but both are five-speed sequentials and the drive found five, so the count stands while the make is not claimed. It was the only five-speed car in its batch; its classmates all selected six.
